findings.claim: Lemma C's sign-indefinite cross term tr(P^2 Q) re-opens the lambda_max/Lindelof branch of the recorded odd-moment no-go (transcript p.80, tx_081), which the proposal's obstruction-evasion section never addresses; the stated remainder form R <= eps*tr A^2 + C(eps)*(trace-asymmetry) does not cover it in the intermediate-depth regime.
findings.argument: tx_081 states the no-go in two parts: (a) an LP certificate p(mu)=c1 mu+c2 mu^2+c3 mu^3 <= 1 on (0,inf) needs c3<=0 and is then dominated by its quadratic part; (b) 'the third moment would help only together with an a-priori bound lambda_max(R~)=O(1), i.e. a pointwise bound for Sum_{n<=X} Lambda(n) n^{-1/2-i tau} on windows of length 1/L' — Lindelof-strength. The proposal evades (a) legitimately (integer-multiplicity cubic via majorization is outside the eigenvalue-valid class; 7.5(g) proves cubic beats quadratic under RH). It never mentions (b). Audit of rank_trace_cubic: with c3<=0, expand tr A^3 = tr P^3 + 3tr(P^2Q) + 3tr(PQ^2) + tr Q^3. tr(PQ^2)>=0 (both PSD) enters with favorable sign c3<0. tr Q^3: I VERIFIED the proposal's odd-trace near-cancellation claim — for a pair block 2m(xx^T-yy^T) with u=x+iy the evaluation vector, ||x||^2-||y||^2 = Re(sum_k u_k^2), and the sub-critical Gabor-Poisson identity gives sum_k phihat(g-tau_k)^2 = l*(phi*phi)(0) EXACTLY for all complex g (the m>=1 aliasing samples of phi*phi at +-l vanish for lambda_w<=1), so the per-block trace asymmetry is O(m*l), depth-independent and sign-definite; hence tr B^3 ~ 3 mu^2 * asym with asym = +2ml*int(phi^2) > 0, and c3<=0 makes tr Q^3 favorable too. The residual danger is exactly tr(P^2 Q) = sum_blocks 2m(||Px||^2 - ||Py||^2): sign-indefinite (no Poisson rigidity — it equals Re sum_{j,j'} m_j m_{j'} <v_j,v_{j'}> l^2 Phi(gamma_j - g)Phi(gamma_{j'} - g), position-dependent complex phases), controllable adversarially by micro-shifting the off-line ordinate by ~pi/(lambda l) to flip the phase of Phi at complex argument. Homogeneity check of the claimed pricing: per deep block |tr(P^2 B)| ~ X^y * l^a (a>=1 from local overlaps, larger with admissible clustering N(t+1)-N(t) ~ log t giving lambda_max(P) ~ l), the block's tr A^2 contribution is ~X^{2y}, and its asymmetry is O(ml). eps*tr A^2 covers only blocks with X^y >= l^a/eps; C(eps)*asym covers only O(l) per block. The intermediate regime X^y ~ polylog with K ~ N/polylog blocks (t2 budget K*X^{2y} <= eta*N respected, remaining traces matched within the o(main) tolerances by adjusting the standard extremal background) yields total unpriced junk ~ N * l^{power} >> the certified gain delta*N. So the Lean-hook statement of rank_trace_cubic with that remainder form is very likely false against the abstract configuration class, and any repair that bounds tr(P^2 Q) for the true zeta multiset appears to need ||P||_op-type control, i.e. the short-window P_X bounds of Remark 7.1(ii) — the known-hard sub-Lindelof threshold. The cited proof-of-concept 7.5(g) is Q-EMPTY (RH-conditional), so it evidences nothing about this term. The proposal's own mitigation (numerics (b) Monte Carlo) measures typical configurations, but validity must hold configuration-by-configuration; the G1-G4 history shows exactly this typical-vs-adversarial gap being fatal. Not scored fatal only because: (i) my l-power bookkeeping in the intermediate regime is a sketch and the campaign has previously produced surprising Poisson rigidities (as with the trace asymmetry) that could yet tame Re(u^T P^2 u); (ii) the proposal gates M3/M4 behind M1+MC and its failure modes name this risk. But the burden is on the proposal: as designed, the certificate arm collides with the recorded no-go's unaddressed branch rather than evading it.

findings.claim: The headline 'mixed-window corner' novelty rests on the paper's crude equal-window accounting (k*lambda<2 => lambda<2/3 at k=3) and is contradicted by the campaign's own sharper record: tx_081 states the odd-moment Fourier support reaches (k-1)*lambda, so k=3 is 'admissible on the whole useful range' lambda<1 with EQUAL windows — the proposal never reconciles the two, and its information-region claim is not new either way.
findings.argument: Shell geometry: the triple-trace functional only probes the sum-zero shell xi1+xi2+xi3=0. For equal windows |xi_i|<=lambda, the maximum of |xi1|+|xi2|+|xi1+xi2| on the shell is 2*lambda (one coordinate must balance the other two, and |xi3|<=lambda caps the balancing), so equal windows at lambda=0.98 already access a region with total support 1.96<2 — a STRICT SUPERSET of the mixed (0.98,0.5,0.5) region, which additionally constrains |xi2|<=0.5. Hence 'one factor at pair-bandwidth ~1, a corner the equal-window analysis never touched' is false at the level of accessible support: mixed windows are a restriction, not an extension, of the equal-window region at lambda_max. What is genuinely at issue is the PROOF range: the proposal's absolute-value MV accounting needs sigma=lambda_a+lambda_b+lambda_c<2 because the far-off-diagonal (|log(n1 n2/n3)| >~ 1, suppressed only by the ~1/(y-z) Dirichlet-kernel tails of the sharp k<d grid cutoff, no rapid decay) carries ell^1 mass ~ sqrt(X_a X_b)*sqrt(X_c) = T^{sigma/2}; tx_081's lambda<1 claim for equal windows would need genuine cancellation there (or relies on its admittedly from-memory RS recall). So either (i) tx_081 is right, and the mixed-window innovation is vacuous — equal windows at lambda->1 already deliver the third trace, which is precisely the situation in which tx_081 then derived the odd-moment no-go — or (ii) the proposal's sigma<2 is the honest boundary, in which case its 'Rudnick-Sarnak boundary re-derived' framing should be presented as the absolute-value-MV boundary and the internal contradiction with the campaign record must be resolved explicitly. The surviving novelty is real but much narrower than claimed: mixed windows enlarge the achievable KERNEL CONE (products Phi_a x Phi_b x Phi_c with three distinct windows, useful for LP rows) within a support region that is not new.

findings.claim: M1's LP overstates the provable data class: it pins every triple row A3(j1,j2) within a uniform tolerance tau3, but T1 delivers only smooth product-kernel functionals Phi_a x Phi_b x Phi_c on the shell, each with its own o(1) error; the go/no-go readout p0^(3)-p0^(2)>0.02 is therefore biased toward 'go', and the M4 certificate cannot consume the rows as priced.
findings.argument: T1 (or RS-type input) yields, per window triple, ONE number: sum_{j1,j2} Phihat_a(j1)Phihat_b(j2)Phihat_c(j1+j2)-weighted combinations of the A3 observables, with an error at the theorem's o(main) scale. Recovering pointwise rows A3(j1,j2)=0 +- tau3 at all ~N^2/2 simplex points requires inverting a tensor-product-cone decomposition (delta-like kernels are not C^3-taper products; the decomposition's ell^1 coefficient mass multiplies the per-instance tolerances), so the certified tolerance at a single grid point degrades by the conditioning of that decomposition — potentially by large factors at N=64-128. An LP whose adversary must match all pointwise rows within a uniform small tau3 is strictly more constrained than one facing only the achievable cone, so p0^(3) computed as designed is an upper bound on the true worth of the upgrade, and the M1 decision gate can pass while the honest (achievable-cone) value collapses toward p0^(2). Likewise the LP dual weights may correspond to a non-achievable kernel, in which case 'the candidate optimal certificate whose validity Lemma C must prove' is not fed by T1 at all. Repair is clean and should be mandatory: parameterize LP rows by the achievable product-kernel cone (mixed windows legitimately enrich it — see finding 2) with propagated tolerances, and re-anchor the 0.02 gate on that LP.

findings.claim: The 'first unconditional correlation theorem for zeta zeros beyond order 2' headline (novelty 1, milestone M2) rests on an unverified negative claim about Rudnick-Sarnak 1996 that the campaign's own record contradicts: tx_081 recalls RS 'prove the n-level correlations are GUE for Sum|xi_j|<2 and state explicitly that RH is not assumed' for zeta.
findings.argument: If RS 1996 (Duke 81) is unconditional for zeta on the full class of test functions with hat-support in Sum|xi_j|<2 — as the tx_081 agent explicitly recalls, and as is consistent with BGSTB24 having targeted only the Montgomery-F(alpha)-specific weighted form at the pair level — then T1's content reduces to: RS's theorem + the (exact, easy) Gabor-Poisson repackaging into mixed Gram traces + explicit error terms, and both novelty claim (1) ('exists in print only under RH') and M2's standalone-headline payoff are wrong. The proposal flags this for verification but nonetheless builds its milestone-payoff structure ('standalone headline theorem... independent of the certificate program's fate') and its BGSTB-analogy framing on the unverified branch. Note the two-sided effect: if RS is unconditional the route's FEASIBILITY improves (the analytic input may be quotable rather than provable-from-scratch, de-risking M2) while the payoff collapses to a technical variant; if RS is conditional, M2 stands but the tx_081-based equal-window claim in finding 2 weakens. Either resolution materially changes the proposal's expected value, and it must be resolved (against the original paper, not memory) before any M2 spend.

findings.claim: The cited proof-of-concept (Section 7.5(g), f(x)=-x^2/9+x^3/18, N_d>=0.85082 under RH) uses the opposite certificate direction from Lemma C: convex f with c3=+1/18>0 consumed via Schur-Horn (sum f(m_j) <= tr f(A)), whereas the proposal's validity polynomial forces c3<=0 and the concave Schur-Jensen direction; 'cubic accounting survives interactions' in the convex direction is automatic majorization and is not evidence about Lemma C's actual content.
findings.argument: psi(m)=c1 m+c2 m^2+c3 m^3+c4*1_{m=1} <= 1 on all integers m>=1 forces c3<=0 (else psi->+inf), and the certificate consumes sum psi(m_j) >= trace-combo - penalties, i.e. the concave/Schur-Jensen direction (which also forces c2<=0 for concavity on [0,inf)). 7.5(g)'s f has positive cubic coefficient and is consumed in the convex/Schur-Horn direction (upper-bounding sum f(m_j) by the trace to penalize high multiplicities). For a single PSD matrix in Gram coordinates both directions are the same diagonal-vs-eigenvalue majorization fact, so the P-only 'survival of interactions' is trivial in both; everything hard in Lemma C is the Q-mixed terms (finding 1), about which 7.5(g) — being Q-empty — says nothing. The citation should be corrected from 'proof-of-concept that cubic accounting survives interactions' to 'proof that a third trace has nonzero certificate value in the Q-free case'; as written it overstates the evidential support for the route's core lemma.

findings.claim: T1's core MV mechanics are sound (verified), but the proposal's 'ratio-type frequencies are handled identically' glosses the one place its own hardest risk lives, and the same-prime-power and near-diagonal bookkeeping deserve one caveat each.
findings.argument: Verified in the proposal's favor: (i) the spacing-weighted MV norms are computed correctly — with coefficients (Lambda*Lambda)(m)/sqrt(m) and delta_m >= 1/(2m), |a_m|^2/delta_m = 2(Lambda*Lambda)(m)^2, and sum_{m<=Y}(Lambda*Lambda)(m)^2 ~ c Y log^3 Y (partial summation over sum_p (log p)^2/p), giving the claimed l^2 T^{sigma/2} = o(T l^3) iff sigma<2; (ii) the near-diagonal band |log(m/n3)|<=1/T is empty since the resonance forces m ~ n3 <= X_c <= T so |m-n3| <= m/T < 1; (iii) exact relations n1 n2 = n3 among prime powers force a common prime, and sum_p (log p)^3 sum_{a,b} p^{-a-b} converges — subleading as claimed; (iv) the three-fold Poisson resummation to the zero side is exact at sub-critical sampling for all lambda_w <= 1 (the aliasing samples of phi*phi at the closed endpoint +-l vanish by continuity). The caveat: the far-off-diagonal is suppressed only by first-order Dirichlet-kernel decay from the sharp k<d grid cutoff (no smooth T-taper is present in the trace), which is exactly why sigma<2 is the absolute-value boundary (finding 2) and why any endpoint improvement or the fallback erosion to sigma<3/2 would shrink both the accessible simplex and the LP value — consistent with, but sharper than, the proposal's own flagged risk.
